Thanks again for the demo last week — Aurelia's architecture review team wants a concise mapping of your third-party operator footprint before we move to security's formal RFP evaluation. Could you provide the following by EOD next week?

Vanessa — I pulled together the vendor roster PDF and annotated access types. Highlights:

- Cloud providers: AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2) — compute & storage; GCP used for EU burst nodes (no KMS access).
- Operator pool: Dedicated operators (managed by Redwood) have ephemeral access to KV caches during inference; we do not persist customer prompt data to operator-controlled storage.
- Partners: Two integration partners (LambdaEdge Integrations, MetricFlow) — both process metadata only; no key access.

Notes / action items:
- We have a planned pilot for an APAC operator node with a third-party operator (Q1 2027). Flagged as "planned" in the roster.
- The SOC2 link we should share is the client-facing redacted report (see Drive link).

I've attached: vendor_roster_master_202611.pdf and a short commentary (redline_sla_aurelia_20261129.docx) with suggested language around operator access and key custody.

— Karthik

Redwood Inference

1) Can you confirm whether any operator/service has long-term access to unredacted customer prompts or outputs? If yes, please specify controls.
2) For planned APAC operator pilot, who is the operator company and what is the timeline for vetting?

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: Maya Singh <m.singh@aurelia-fin.com>, Lucas Price <l.price@vendor-assess.com>, procurement@aurelia-fin.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Third-party operator clarity checklist request — completed roster + questionnaire answers

Maya / Lucas — attaching the completed roster and our inline answers to the short questionnaire. Summary answers (top-level):

- Long-term access to unredacted prompts/outputs: No. Operator nodes may handle data in-memory during inference; we do not persist or index customer prompts on operator-controlled storage. KV caches are ephemeral and encrypted; access is restricted by role-based policies.
- APAC operator pilot: ThirdPartyOps Pty Ltd (Australia) — pilot planned for Jan 2027, limited to non-production traffic for 8 weeks while we complete their security checklist. We've marked them as "planned" in the vendor roster.
- Key custody: Customers can choose Redwood-managed KMS (we use AWS KMS/HSM) or bring-your-own KMS (BYOK). When customers use BYOK, Redwood does not hold the key materials.

Attachments included:
- vendor_roster_master_202611.pdf (vendor roles + access types + region flags)
- aurelia_followup_questions_20261201_filled.pdf (inline answers)
- link to redacted SOC2 report & encryption summary in Drive (see link below)

Next steps: happy to schedule a 30-min call with security to walk through any controls or runbook items. If acceptable, we'll also add a short supplemental clause to your SLA indicating operator access constraints and the BYOK option.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
